data.narrative: Learner demonstrated outstanding system architecture and web security discipline, selecting prefix routing for clean namespace segregation, constructing fail-fast Pydantic URL validators, and enforcing defense-in-depth scheme validation at the redirect egress boundary.

dimension_scores.observation: Selected prefix route (/r/{code}) with clear understanding of route collision hazards and operational namespace isolation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Option A keeps redirects separate from health checks, documentation, and management endpoints, so user-generated codes cannot collide with internal routes.

dimension_scores.observation: Quickly diagnosed security regression to relaxed LinkCreate schema validation and designed defense-in-depth egress checks.
dimension_scores.evidence: The likely cause is that the LinkCreate validation was removed, weakened, bypassed, or no longer used by POST /links... We should also add a defense-in-depth check before redirecting.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified stored XSS attack vectors (javascript:, data:, userinfo @, backslashes) and articulated the superiority of explicit allowlists over denylists.
dimension_scores.evidence: An allowlist follows the safer rule: if it is not explicitly approved, reject it... This blocks javascript:, data:, file:, and unknown future schemes automatically.

dimension_scores.observation: Maintained strict HTTP semantics, explaining why validation failures must return 400 rather than polluting 500 server error telemetry.
dimension_scores.evidence: A 500 would falsely suggest a server failure and trigger unnecessary incident investigation, while 200 would imply that the malicious input was accepted successfully.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered structured, precise technical explanations with concrete curl verification proof across all endpoints and attack vectors.
dimension_scores.evidence: Provided exact status codes (200, 201, 307, 404, 400) and correlated them to architectural invariants and mitigation strategies.

strengths: Robust threat modeling and defense-in-depth validation across both API ingress and redirect egress layers
Deep grasp of HTTP semantics, namespace isolation, and production observability hygiene
growth_areas: Extend this API layer with token-based authentication and role-based access control in Module 04
data.recommendation: In Module 04, implement JWT authentication and scoped authorization to secure the /links management routes while keeping /r/{code} public.

concepts_demonstrated: Stored XSS prevention and open redirect defense
Pydantic v2 input validation and custom exception handlers
Client IP hashing and audit logging

public_evidence.artifact: FastAPI Core CRUD & Public Redirect Service
public_evidence.student_action: Architected prefix routing (/r/{code}), implemented strict Pydantic URL sanitization with scheme allowlisting, and built defense-in-depth redirect handler.
public_evidence.technical_detail: FastAPI endpoints POST /links, GET /links/{id}, GET /r/{code} with Pydantic validators, custom 400 exception handler, and append-only ClickEvent recording.
public_evidence.proof: Executed test_validation_regression.py (12/12 passed) and test_redirect_defense.py; verified curl outputs for 200 health, 201 creation, 307 redirect, 404 not found, and 400 rejection across 9 attack vectors.
public_evidence.ability: Builds abuse-resistant REST APIs and hardened redirect services
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves the engineer defends against stored XSS, open redirects, and route collisions while maintaining rigorous HTTP semantics.
